rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

positions.name: Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bull 3X
positions.catalyst: Soft June CPI is the dominant fresh macro catalyst driving today's tape. Headline CPI fell 0.4% m/m and annual inflation slowed to 3.5% vs 3.8% expected (reported 7/14), collapsing the near-term Fed-hike odds that had been hanging over the market. The tape has flipped risk-on: the July 15 Polymarket contract implies a 73% probability the S&P opens higher, bank earnings are beating broadly (JPM/BAC beat, MS/BLK/JNJ/UAL reporting today), and the oil escalation that dominated this week is now FADING — Trump abandoned the 20% Strait of Hormuz cargo fee and WTI is up only ~0.45% today after +3.3% yesterday, removing an inflation overhang. SPXL is +0.44% pre-open (276.85 last / 277.05x277.14 book, Robinhood live 11:42Z), unextended and clean.
positions.driver: Playing the dovish-CPI risk-on with the broadest, least-extended 3x on the board. The catalyst (a soft inflation print that removes Fed-hike fear) is market-WIDE, so I want diversified index beta, not a single-sector bet. 3x is justified by a strong, fresh macro catalyst, and applying it to the S&P — the most diversified underlying available — gives the leverage the lowest single-name blow-up risk. SPXL at +0.44% pre is nowhere near the no-chase band, so entry quality is good. RUNNERS-UP: SOXL (3x semis) rejected as a chase — it is +4.2% pre-open, this is DAY 2 of the semis bounce, the 3x is running hot versus its own underlying (SMH only +1.15%), and sector leader MU has already faded to -0.5% pre-market, i.e. the move is decelerating and buying 3x into a fading Day-2 bounce is exactly the trap flagged yesterday. TQQQ (3x Nasdaq, +1.5% pre) rejected — the dovish-CPI growth tailwind is real, but IBM is -22% pre on a Q2 revenue miss and slashed guidance, sparking an AI/SaaS 'SaaSpocalypse' scare that is a direct, concentrated headwind for the Nasdaq; SPXL captures the same rate tailwind with far less of that idiosyncratic tech dispersion. FAS (3x financials, +0.6% pre) rejected — bank beats are supportive but the tape shows no real momentum in the group and MS/BLK report today, so it is a coin-flip event bet. BITX (2x BTC, +0.24%) rejected — flat, no catalyst.
positions.risks: This is a leveraged long into a gap-up open, so I am buying a market that is already 73% expected to open green — if the open is the high and CPI relief is 'sell the news,' 3x amplifies the fade. The live idiosyncratic risk is IBM's -22% guidance miss metastasizing into a broader 'AI capex digestion' fear that drags the whole index intraday; the S&P's diversification is the mitigant but not immunity. Oil is a two-way wildcard — Brent still ~$85 and any fresh Hormuz escalation re-arms the inflation trade and pressures multiples. Hard stop 249.43 (-10% on the 3x, i.e. a ~3.3% S&P drawdown) sized as a disaster stop that only triggers on a genuine risk-off reversal, not intraday chop.
